Zhuoyuan Hao (Larry Hao / 郝卓远)

Website · Publications · Google Scholar · X · CV · hzy2210@gmail.com

I publish papers as Zhuoyuan Hao and use Larry Hao professionally; both names refer to the same person.

Finished my CS degree at HITSZ in three years (2023–2026), now an MPhil student at HKUST. I study the mechanisms behind LLM reasoning: why models reason the way they do, and how RL post-training quietly breaks them. Outside research I contribute upstream a lot: 87 merged PRs across 17 repositories, plus code co-authored with maintainers.

Research

Echo of Prompt · first author, ICLR 2026. Reasoning models almost always restate the question to themselves before they start reasoning. Everyone filed this under "SFT artifact." It's more than that: the echo re-anchors attention and keeps a long chain of thought from drifting, and models pay for it when it's missing. I show the probabilistic cost, trace the information flow, and turn the effect into a prompt-time trick that beats baseline under a fixed token budget. → evidence page · code · OpenReview

Reward Hacking in Rubric-based RL (CHERRL) · co-first author. When an LLM judge hands out the reward, the policy can learn to exploit the judge's blind spots instead of actually improving. We built a controllable sandbox: inject a known bias, reproduce the hack cleanly, and pin down the exact step it starts. Then an agent reads the training logs and flags that onset on its own. → project summary · code · arXiv
